user.title: Set up Garden Irrigation
user.description: Select the weather entity used for forecasts (temperature factor and rain veto). Everything else — circuits, notifications, tuning — is configured afterwards via the integration's Configure dialog.

abort.already_configured: Already configured — only one hub is supported.

data.regen_sensor: Rain sensor, mm over the last 24 h (optional)
data.notaus_minuten: Emergency-stop threshold (must exceed every max duration)

data_description.regen_sensor: Must provide a ROLLING 24-hour sum, not a daily total: a daily total resets to 0 at midnight, so in the morning yesterday evening's rain is missing — exactly when the veto decides. If your sensor delivers something else (mm per measurement interval, a cumulative counter or a rate in mm/h), build the rolling value with a statistics helper and max_age 24 h; FAQ question 4 has a ready-made recipe for all three shapes. Leaving it empty is fine too — then only forecast rain counts.

benachrichtigungen.title: Notifications
benachrichtigungen.description: Choose the services that receive the daily plan, alarms and reports. Custom entries are allowed in case a service is not loaded right now.

data_description.notify_dienste: Pick from the notify services registered on this system — usually `notify.mobile_app_<your-phone>`. Empty = no pushes, on purpose. After saving, press the “Test notification” button: it reports the outcome as a notice inside Home Assistant, even when nothing is configured.

tuning.title: Tuning
tuning.description: All defaults come from the proven 4-zone reference system — they work without any changes. Each field is explained below it; to play with the score formula, try the [interactive calculator]({rechner_url}) on the project page.

gewichte.name: Score weights & thresholds
gewichte.description: The score (0–100) blends three factors — soil moisture, temperature/evapotranspiration, days waited — weighted and normalised to the weight sum. The score maps linearly onto each circuit's min–max watering duration.

data_description.score_gewicht_boden: How much dry soil counts. The factor rises 2 points per percentage point below the circuit's veto threshold — circuits without a soil sensor skip it (the other weights take over).
data_description.score_gewicht_temp: How much warm or high-evaporation days count. Choose the source (Tmax or ET₀) in the "Temperature & evapotranspiration" section.
data_description.score_gewicht_tage: How much the wait since the last watering counts — prevents a zone from being starved for weeks in mild weather.
data_description.score_skip_schwelle: If a circuit's daily score is below this, it is skipped today (0 min).
data_description.score_tage_saettigung: After this many days without watering the days factor reaches 100%.

temperatur.name: Temperature & evapotranspiration (ET₀)
temperatur.description: The temperature factor can use the classic maximum temperature (Tmax over the next 3 days) or the estimated reference evapotranspiration ET₀ (Hargreaves) — sun position from latitude + day of year, Tmax/Tmin from the forecast, no extra sensors needed. ET₀ shines for lawns: sunny, dry days evaporate far more than Tmax alone suggests. The current value is in the attributes of `sensor.garten_plan_heute` (et0_mm) — check it before switching.

data_description.score_temp_quelle: Tmax = kit default. ET₀ = evapotranspiration estimate; falls back to Tmax automatically when templow values are missing.
data_description.score_temp_anker: Tmax mode only: at this maximum temperature the factor is 0.
data_description.score_temp_spanne: Tmax mode only: this many degrees above the anchor give factor 100 (default: 100 at 30 °C).
data_description.score_et0_anker: ET₀ mode only: at this evapotranspiration (mm/day) the factor is 0. 2 mm ≈ cool, overcast day.
data_description.score_et0_spanne: ET₀ mode only: this many mm/day above the anchor give factor 100. Default: 100 at 7 mm/day (hot midsummer day).
data_description.score_forecast_typ: daily = your weather integration's daily forecast (default). Use hourly only if it offers no daily forecast.

regen_sonne.name: Rain & sun
regen_sonne.description: Two rain vetoes force the watering duration to 0; the peak-sun lockout defers pot doses during harsh midday sun.

data_description.regen_beobachtet_mm: This much measured rain within 24 h cancels the run. Only active with a configured rain-24h sensor (Global settings).
data_description.regen_forecast_mm: This much rain forecast for today cancels the run.
data_description.strahlung_schwelle: Above this reading of your solar-radiation sensor, pot doses are deferred. Unit = your sensor's; without a sensor it has no effect.

toepfe.name: Pot frequency watering
toepfe.description: Pot/drip circuits get small top-up doses during the day to keep the soil inside its target band. These limits cap frequency and volume — no matter what the sensors report.

data.topf_batterie_min: Pause pot doses below sensor battery

data_description.topf_max_dosen: Upper limit per pot circuit and day — also caps the daily water volume.
data_description.topf_dosis_max_min: A single dose never runs longer, however dry the sensor reads.
data_description.topf_min_intervall_min: Wait until the soil has absorbed the previous dose and the sensor has caught up.
data_description.topf_glitch_grenze: Readings below this count as sensor glitches (e.g. 0% on a radio dropout) and never trigger a dose.
data_description.topf_dosen_von: Quiet hours for pot doses. The peak-sun lockout only guards against blazing sun — at night solar radiation is 0 and the gate is wide open, so without a time window the controller waters at 3 a.m. if soil moisture says so. The main evening run is unaffected.
data_description.topf_dosen_bis: End of the dosing window. A window across midnight (end before start) is allowed.
data_description.topf_batterie_min: If a battery configured on the circuit drops below this, no more doses are given. Reason: a soil sensor with an empty battery does not report nothing — it reports a downward-drifting value, so the controller would think the pot is bone dry and water at full tilt forever. 0 disables the check.

kosten.name: Water costs
kosten.description: Only used by the cost sensors of circuits with a flow sensor.

data_description.wasser_tarif: Price per cubic metre of water per your utility.
data_description.waehrung: Display unit of the cost sensors (e.g. EUR, CHF).

data.name: Circuit name
data.bodensensoren: Soil moisture sensors (optional, several = minimum wins)

data_description.gruppe_reihenfolge: Sort weight, not an exclusive slot: duplicate numbers are fine (ties break alphabetically). Sets the chain position of sequential circuits and the anchor for "parallel from order position"; has no effect for "parallel from run start". Gaps (10/20/30) leave room to insert later.
data_description.ausfuehrung: Sequential: joins the order chain (circuits run one after another — e.g. sprinklers sharing water pressure). Parallel from run start: starts immediately with the run. Parallel from order position: starts when the chain reaches the sequential circuit with the same (or next higher) number — e.g. a drip zone coupled to the second sprinkler. Without a matching position it starts with the run.

data.veto_schwelle: Soil veto threshold (moist enough above this)
data.k_faktor: Dose response k (%-points per minute at 50 % soil)
data.block_max_min: Cycle-and-soak: max. minutes at a time (0 = off)

data_description.temp_quelle: Overrides the global tuning setting for this circuit only — e.g. ET₀ for a lawn zone without a soil sensor while the rest stays on Tmax.
data_description.flow_sensor: Needs an INCREASING meter reading in m³ or liters (unit auto-detected) — NOT the instantaneous flow rate (m³/h, L/min). Turn a rate into a meter with an Integral helper: Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → Integral, method “left” — recipe in the FAQ. A wrong sensor type shows up as 0.0 L after watering.
data_description.block_max_min: Cycle-and-soak: splits a long run into blocks so the water can soak in instead of running off — needed whenever your sprinkler applies water faster than the soil absorbs it (the rule on clay and slopes). Pick the minutes so that at most 5-8 mm (clay) or 8-12 mm (loam) fall per block; FAQ 20 has the formula. 0 = one continuous run. Must stay below the emergency-stop threshold, which counts per block. Note: this changes HOW the water is applied, not HOW MUCH — the amount comes from Max duration above.
data_description.block_pause_min: Waiting time between blocks so the water can soak in. 30 minutes is a good default, more on heavy clay. Careful: the pauses stretch the run — three blocks with 30-minute pauses finish an hour later than the pure watering time suggests.
data_description.k_faktor: How strongly the pot reacts to one minute of water: how many percentage points soil moisture rises per watering minute (measured at 50 %). The dose length is derived from it. You don't need the formula, only the direction: doses too short and the pot stays dry → lower k. Overshooting the target band → raise k. To measure it yourself: water for a known time, note the soil value before and the peak 1–2 h after, then k = rise ÷ (minutes × (100 − soil before) ÷ 100). A small pot on a strong dripper easily reaches 20+, a large planter sits at 1–3.

data_description.gruppe_reihenfolge: Sort weight, not an exclusive slot: duplicate numbers are fine (ties break alphabetically). Sets the chain position of sequential circuits and the anchor for "parallel from order position"; has no effect for "parallel from run start". Gaps (10/20/30) leave room to insert later.
data_description.ausfuehrung: Sequential: joins the order chain (circuits run one after another — e.g. sprinklers sharing water pressure). Parallel from run start: starts immediately with the run. Parallel from order position: starts when the chain reaches the sequential circuit with the same (or next higher) number — e.g. a drip zone coupled to the second sprinkler. Without a matching position it starts with the run.

jetzt_bewaessern.name: Jetzt bewässern
jetzt_bewaessern.description: Startet den geplanten Bewässerungslauf sofort (Skip/Urlaub gelten weiter).

not_aus.name: Not-Aus
not_aus.description: Bricht den Lauf ab und schließt alle Ventile mit Wiederholversuchen.

plan_neu_berechnen.name: Plan neu berechnen
plan_neu_berechnen.description: Berechnet Score und Tagesdauer aller Kreise sofort neu (inkl. Topf-Nach-Check).

dosis_geben.name: Dosis geben
dosis_geben.description: Löst sofort eine Topf-Dose aus (umgeht Score-Gates, respektiert Sicherheits-Basics).

raten_sensor.title: Water meter sensor for “{kreis}” is a flow RATE
raten_sensor.description:
The configured water meter sensor `{sensor}` reports a flow rate ({einheit}) instead of a cumulative meter reading. Session liters cannot be measured this way — 0 L is recorded per session.

Fix: select a cumulative water meter sensor, or create an Integral helper on top of your rate sensor (Settings → Devices & services → Helpers → Integral) and select that helper as the water meter sensor. See FAQ question 17 for the step-by-step recipe.

notify_dienst_fehlt.title: Notification service “{dienst}” does not exist
notify_dienst_fehlt.description:
Irrigation is configured to notify via `{dienst}`, but that service does not exist on this system — so **no push is sent**.

Usual causes: a typo, or the phone was set up again and the Companion app service is now named differently. Find the correct name under Developer tools → Actions (search for “notify”) and enter it under Configure → Notifications. The “Test notification” button verifies it immediately.
